teaser.text: Adobe sells software that helps people create content, handle documents, and run digital marketing. Its business is built mainly on recurring access fees, but understanding a dollar requires following it from customer commitment to delivery cost and profit.

stock.title: Adobe stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Adobe's stock forecast weighs a $287.73 path by October 2027 against bear and bull cases, cash generation, and valuation.
stock.opening: Adobe’s weighted forecast reaches $287.73 by October 2027 (+14%) and hinges on converting free reach and AI demand into profitable growth without losing cash-generation strength. Adobe must turn reach and AI into paid growth while preserving margins, cash, and financial flexibility.
stock.closing: The full Adobe memo also answers how Adobe’s business works, how its rivals compare, how management is changing, and what risks could alter the outcome.

paragraphs.text: The weighted path reaches $287.73 by October 2027, $365.66 by October 2028 and $471.33 by October 2029, including dividends. That means returns of 14%, 45% and 87% from today’s $251.67.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Adobe, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: The bear case starts at $7,560 million, falls to $6,793 million and ends at $6,888 million. It assumes weaker revenue and margins as cheaper tools, downgrades and hosting costs pressure conversion. The bull case rises from $10,065 million to $11,900 million and then $13,825 million, as Firefly, Acrobat AI and enterprise products convert free reach into paid demand. Creative freemium monthly active users already exceeded 100 million and grew more than 70% year over year, but paid conversion and AI gross profit remain undisclosed.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Adobe really make?

paragraphs.text: Operating cash flow was $10,031 million. After $179 million of capital spending, free cash flow was $9,852 million. That equals 41.4% of revenue and shows unusually strong cash conversion.

Stock compensation is another economic claim. Adobe recorded $1,942 million of stock compensation in FY2025. Because no cash leaves when shares are granted, accounting adds the expense back to operating cash flow. But existing shareholders bear dilution, or the cost of repurchasing shares to offset it. Subtracting stock compensation leaves analytical “real free cash flow” of $7,910 million.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Adobe today?

paragraphs.text: P/E, or price-to-earnings, compares the share price with earnings per share. Trailing P/E uses the last twelve months; forward P/E uses an estimate for the next twelve months. GAAP earnings include required expenses, while Adobe’s non-GAAP measure removes specified items such as stock compensation and intangible amortization. The two earnings definitions produce very different apparent prices, so the forward multiple needs an accounting check before it can be called cheap.

earnings.title: Adobe earnings: guidance and what to watch
earnings.meta_description: Adobe reports on December 9, 2026; guidance points to revenue, ARR and earnings targets, while AI monetization is the key test.
earnings.opening: Adobe's next results are due on December 9, 2026. Watch whether Adobe turns AI features into paid adoption without weakening margins.
earnings.closing: The full memo also answers questions about Adobe's business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: What has Adobe guided for fiscal 2026?

paragraphs.text: Adobe expects full-year revenue of $26,576–$26,626 million. Its fourth-quarter target is $6,800–$6,850 million. The split between Business Professionals & Consumers and Creative & Marketing Professionals helps separate demand for everyday documents from demand for creative and marketing tools.

GAAP is the standard accounting result. Adobe expects fiscal 2026 diluted earnings per share of $18.12–$18.17 under GAAP and $24.45–$24.50 on an adjusted basis, which removes selected costs. The adjustment includes $5.42 per share for stock-based and deferred compensation. Shares preserve cash when used as pay, but dilute existing owners, so adjusted earnings are not the same as cash available to spend.

blocks.heading: What do Adobe's last eight quarters show?

paragraphs.text: Q3 FY2026 combined faster revenue growth and strong cash generation with weaker margins and smaller recurring additions.
Profit grew more slowly. Gross margin fell to 88.7% from 89.3%. Operating income rose 8.3% to $2,354 million, producing a 34.8% operating margin against about 36.3% a year earlier.

blocks.heading: What should I watch in Adobe's next results?

paragraphs.text: Adobe MAX, scheduled for November 10–12, 2026, is the next clear product test. Investors should look for released AI features with clear access and pricing, not only demonstrations. Topaz and the wider AI programme must make customers’ work easier, then turn that usefulness into paid adoption.
